events.title: Diocletian Proclaimed Roman Emperor
events.description: Diocletian was chosen as emperor by the army. His rise ended decades of turmoil known as the Crisis of the Third Century.
events.significance: Diocletian restored order and split the administration of the empire. His reforms shaped Roman government for generations.

events.title: Nuremberg Trials Begin
events.description: Twenty-four surviving leaders of Nazi Germany went on trial before an International Military Tribunal in the Palace of Justice in Nuremberg.
events.significance: The trials set a precedent that leaders can be held personally accountable for war crimes and crimes against humanity. They helped shape modern international criminal law.

events.title: UN Adopts the Declaration of the Rights of the Child
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly unanimously adopted a declaration setting out the rights and protections every child should enjoy.
events.significance: The declaration laid the groundwork for the later Convention on the Rights of the Child. It established children's welfare as a global concern.

events.title: Microsoft Releases Windows 1.0
events.description: Microsoft launched the first version of Windows. It was a graphical interface that ran on top of MS-DOS.
events.significance: Windows 1.0 was the first step toward the operating system that came to dominate personal computing.

events.title: First International Space Station Module Launched
events.description: The Russian-built Zarya module lifted off from Kazakhstan, becoming the first component of the International Space Station.
events.significance: The launch began the assembly of the largest structure humans have built in orbit. It started a long-running partnership among space agencies.
